detail.readme:
# MP Manager A free dual pane, Material Design file manager for Android with focus on APKs and the goal to be an open source alternative to MT Manager

[![GitHub Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/AbdurazaaqMohammed/MP-Manager?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&label=Download&color=purple)](https://github.com/AbdurazaaqMohammed/MP-Manager/releases) [![Telegram Discussion](https://img.shields.io/badge/Telegram%20Discussion-2CA5E0?style=for-the-badge&logo=telegram&logoColor=white)](https://t.me/MP_Manager_Discussion) [![Donate](https://img.shields.io/badge/Donate-0079C1?style=for-the-badge&logo=paypal)](https://paypal.me/AbdurazaaqMohammed) ## Features ### File Manager
Dual pane navigation

Browse two folders side by side. This makes it easy to move or copy files from one pane to the other. A separate home folder can be set for each pane. The active pane can be highlighted with a colored border, optionally animated. There are back and forward buttons, button to sync both panes to the same folder, new file/folder button, parent folder button. You can pull down to refresh the current folder.
Bookmarks and history Add any folder to bookmarks and manage them from a bottom drawer. The drawer has tabs for bookmarks and navigation history and opens by swiping up on the bottom bar. Bookmarks can be organized into groups, edited, and deleted by long pressing on one. You can choose which tab new bookmarks go to, and optionally show bookmarks and bookmark groups in the sidebar.


Bookmarks and history drawer

Filtering, sorting and hidden files Filter the current folder as you type. Sort by name, size, date or type, reverse order, and choose whether a sort applies only to the current folder or everywhere. You can hide files from the list, show or hide system hidden files such as dot folders, and edit the list of manually hidden files later.


Filter the current folder  ·  Choose a sorting mode  ·  Hide files from the list

Advanced search Search the current folder by file name and optionally recurse into subfolders. Advanced options include match case, regular expressions, searching for text inside file contents, and minimum or maximum file size. Recent searches are saved for quick reuse. Content search can also be run over an entire folder from the menu, reporting the number of matches in each file. A list of paths can be set to be excluded from searching. Search also works inside ZIP and APK archives, and results are shown in an MT Manager style dialog with a persistent results pane. The results dialog stays open while you work, keeps its scroll position, and lets you save edits back into the APK.


The advanced search dialog

File operations Create files and folders, rename, copy, move and delete with progress reporting. Extract, add files in ZIP, APK. Compression option when modifying ZIPS + auto sign and zipalign for APKs. Rename several files at once using templates with prefix, suffix, numbering and find/replace. When a destination file already exists, each conflict can be resolved with replace, skip or rename, applied to all remaining files, or added to an existing archive. Copies can keep the original modification date. Renaming several files previews the new names before they are applied, and in multi select mode swiping across two files selects every file between them. The MIME type detected from the file contents is shown before sharing or opening a file, and a default app can be set or cleared for a file type. Files received from other apps can be saved from the share menu. Unknown files can be opened with a custom app from the Open with dialog. Archives and backups can be browsed directly, including nested archives spanned across folders. PDF files open in a built-in viewer. MIUI and Android backup (.bak) archives are supported, and .bak files are handled by their original extension.


File shared with app

Shell scripts can be viewed, edited or executed with the output and exit code shown, optionally with root.


Shell script output

File properties and sharing View type, size and last modified date, and copy any value to the clipboard with a long press. Share files or open them with another app. With root, file permissions can be edited, including owner, group, the read, write and execute bits for each, and the setuid, setgid and sticky flags. Checksums can be computed for any file, pasted hashes can be verified, and hashes of two files can be compared. ZIP entries have CRC32 and checksum support.


Properties

Root and Shizuku file management Browse and manage files with root or Shizuku, including Android/data, obb and media on Android 11+. With Shizuku you can also open other locations the shell can read but the app cannot, such as /storage/emulated and system folders, read-only where modification is not permitted. Root listing is cached for speed, commands are safe on paths with spaces, and editors write back through root when needed. In root or Shizuku mode the root directory is added to the sidebar.


Viewing /Android/data and /data/data with root

DocumentsProvider viewer Browse app data folders through the Storage Access Framework without root. DocumentsProviders on the device are listed in a dedicated tool (Tools → Documents providers), and a provider can be opened in a pane like a regular folder. Useful for reaching /Android/data and other locations granted via providers, including ones injected by patchers.
WebDAV and SMB network storage Open **Network connections** from the sidebar: one Material-tabbed dialog contains **FTP**, **WebDAV**, and **SMB**. The SMB tab automatically discovers local servers using advertisements, Windows WS-Discovery, and a bounded SMB2/3 scan. WebDAV accepts HTTP(S) collection URLs; SMB accepts `smb://server/share` with an optional custom port and domain/workgroup. SMB1 is not supported. Create files/folders, rename, delete, and copy or move files and whole folders between a network location and the other pane. Saved connections are encrypted with Android Keystore. Existing destinations are not silently overwritten, and moves remove their source only after a successful transfer. Opening a network file downloads a local copy for the built-in viewers and editors; edits are not automatically synced back. See [Network storage](docs/NETWORK_STORAGE.md) for usage, limitations, and tests. FTP, WebDAV and SMB use the normal file-list icons, spacing and customizable Material long-press menu, without downloading thumbnails. Save configurations without connecting and pin any protocol in the sidebar **Storage** section. Server-reported quotas/volume space are shown when available; unknown totals are never guessed.
Customizable file menu Reorder the long press file menu by dragging items anywhere. The menu can be shown as a bottom sheet or in two columns, with Material colors.


File menu order

### Media
Built-in audio and video player Play audio and video files without leaving the app. A mini player dialog with artwork, seek bar and playback controls can play in the background or expand into a full player. Player settings allow the screen to be kept on while playing and the skip duration to be changed.
Image viewer Open images with swipe between pictures in directory. EXIF metadata is shown for supported files, images can be deleted or shared from the viewer. The built-in image editor can crop single or multiple images with standard or lossless JPEG quality, and view or edit EXIF tags in single or batch mode. The editor also rotates and flips images, crops to a custom aspect ratio, and strips EXIF and other metadata from JPEG files.


Image viewer and editor

### APK Tools
APK information and install Tap an APK to see its icon, name, version code and name, package name, signature schemes used (V1, V2, V3, V4) and whether it is protected. The full signature details can be shown on press. You can view files inside the APK and more features outlined below. Installing both regular and split APKS is supported. For installed packages APK and data directory are also shown with root.


The APK info dialog

Sign APK and split APKs Sign APKs and split APKs with your own or default (Debug) key. Signing supports JKS and PKCS12 keystores as well as PK8/PEM keys, and new keys can be generated inside the app. Automatic signing after modifying an APK can be toggled and configured. For safety with keys that have passwords, it is required to authenticate each time before signing but biometrics can be used as alternative to entering password every time.


Signature settings

Toast/Dialog Maker Add a Toast or dialog message to activities in an APK, or remove all Toast calls from an APK at once by patching smali code.
Decompile, build and protect All functions from [REAndroid APKEditor](https://github.com/REAndroid/APKEditor) are available: Decompile an APK, Build an APK from a decompiled folder, merge (AntiSplit), Refactor obfuscated resource names and Protect. When merging split APKs the splits to include can be chosen, device specific splits can be kept or dropped, a compression level can be set, and the merged APK can be signed automatically. Other tools options can also be configured before starting.


Decompiling

Quick edit APK attributes Change the launcher icon, app name, install location, version code and name, min SDK and target SDK quickly in a dialog. Every activity and property in the manifest can also be edited from a tree view, including disabling entries. A .bak backup is created upon edit and can be restored.


Fast edit attributes

APK optimization and cloning Optimize APKs by removing chosen files, with a default list of common tracker and metadata files that can be edited. You can [clone an APK](https://github.com/developer-krushna/ApkCloner) with a new package name.


The clone APK dialog

Dex editing Edit dex files with [DEX Editor Pro](https://github.com/developer-krushna/Dex-Editor-Android) by developer-krushna. When editing a dex file inside an APK you can choose which dex files to load. Saving asks whether to add the modified file back into the APK and sign it, and a .bak backup is created upon modifying an APK. Search is improved with find usages, find overriding methods and Clear method actions.


Choose which dex files to load  ·  The integrated dex editor

ARSC editing Edit resources.arsc with the built-in ARSC Editor or ARSC Editor Plus. Search by resource value or ID, copy IDs, jump to an ID, browse the string pool and TEXT tab, with automatic backups on save. ARSC Editor Plus also provides a translation mode for editing values side by side, adding and deleting entries, and batch import and export of entries and whole string pools from files or another archive. A floating resource querier looks up a resource by name or ID, checks a color written as #RGB, #ARGB, #RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB, and converts numbers between binary, octal, decimal and hex.


ARSC Editor  ·  ARSC Editor Plus

Xposed patcher Patch an APK with [LSPatch](https://github.com/JingMatrix/LSPatch) in integrated mode: an Xposed loader is embedded so the selected modules run standalone without a manager app. Embed module APKs, choose a signature bypass level, configure options (DocumentsProvider injection, fake-signature, GMS replacement, forcing cleartext traffic, overriding target SDK or version code and more), and save/load patch profiles. The output is signed with the key configured under Sign Settings.
APK data multiplexing Multiplex (deduplicate) an APK by redirecting entries that are byte-identical to entries inside the stored embedded APK, so duplicated data is stored only once and the file shrinks. The output is signed in place with the V2/V3 raw-file signer using your key, preserving the optimization.
IL2CPP runtime dumper Dump Unity IL2CPP games at runtime without root or hooking. Injects libil2cppdumper.so into the APK, loaded from a chosen class's static initializer. When the patched app runs, it waits for the IL2CPP runtime to initialize, then writes a C#-like dump of every managed type (dump.cs) plus IDA/Ghidra scripts (script.json). The dump can be exposed through a DocumentsProvider for easy browsing.
Native library patcher Patch native .so libraries with instruction stubs (port of LibPatcher) so a function returns a fixed value: boolean true/false, integer zero/max, long zero/-1, float/double zero, or void (NOP). Enter hex offsets from Ghidra, IDA or r2. Only armeabi-v7a and arm64-v8a are supported.
### Editing and Comparing
Text editor A full text editor based on [Sora Editor](https://github.com/Rosemoe/sora-editor) with a customizable bottom bar, regex find and replace, and many editor features. Multiple files can be open at once in tabs. Syntax highlighting, jump to line, line actions such as duplicate, delete and case conversion, comment toggling, word wrap, a read only mode and a method and field list are available, and click, long press and extra button actions can be configured. Binary Android XML (AXML) files can be decoded for editing and re-encoded on save automatically. A plain XML file that looks like a compiled manifest or resource file is detected as such and can be saved back as binary AXML.


Editing a decoded AXML file

Hex editor View and edit any file in hex with goto offset, search, and selectable encodings. Changes can be saved back directly. Data can be pasted from hex, decimal, binary, ASCII or base64 text, values can be searched and replaced as string, integer or other data types in either endianness, and unsaved changes can be reverted.


Hex editor

Compare tools Compare two text files, two ZIP/APK files, two resources.arsc files, or two dex files. Select one item in each pane and the matching compare option appears in the file menu. Dex comparison summarizes added, removed and changed classes, can ignore debug information, compilation optimizations, register counts and nop instructions, hides classes by category, and shows differences side by side or unified with navigation between them.


Comparing DEX  ·  Diff view of file

### APK Extractor
Extract and share APK parts Extract APKs in batch and pull out specific parts: the app icon, resources.arsc, classes.dex, AndroidManifest.xml, base.apk, splits and native libs, as well as the launch activity. Split APKs can be merged into a single APK before extracting, and anything can be shared directly. Pull down to refresh the app list, with extra features when root is available. Installed apps can also be launched through an activity picker, force stopped, disabled or enabled, have their data cleared or be uninstalled with root.


App info  ·  Extration options

### FTP
FTP server Use FTP server with custom port, username and password, with optional FTPS explicit or implicit TLS. The server keeps a notification while running so it can be stopped easily. Connection settings can be saved as profiles, and the device IP can be copied or shared.


The FTP server dialog

FTP client Use the **FTP** tab in **Network connections** to connect to an FTP server with optional FTPS and browse remote folders in either pane. Files can be uploaded from the device, and connection details can be saved as profiles and pinned under sidebar Storage. Existing FTP profiles remain compatible.


The FTP client dialog

### AI / MCP
MCP Service (AI tools) MP Manager ships a built-in **MCP (Model Context Protocol) server**, similar to MT Manager's MCP feature but specialized for APKs: connect any MCP-capable AI tool (ChatMCP, Claude, Cherry Studio, …) and drive the app's file, ZIP and APK engines through conversation. You describe what you want; the AI calls MP Manager's tools. Start it from the sidebar ("MCP Service") or the Tools hub. It serves: - **Streamable HTTP** at `http://:8787/mcp` (and legacy **SSE** at `http://:8787/sse`) — on-device AI tools use `127.0.0.1`, tools on a computer use the LAN address shown while running. - **`mp_file_*` tools** — browse, read (text + paged binary), create/edit/search/append, find-and-replace (literal or regex), byte-level patching, truncation, mkdir, copy/move/rename and permanent delete, upload (AI device → phone) / download (phone → AI device), and access-policy queries (what the AI may touch, and why). - **`mp_zip_*` tools** — list and read entries without extracting, integrity checks (with password), create archives with compression level 0–9 and optional AES password, add/replace/delete/rename entries, extract whole archives or single entries. (Password-protected write/extract needs Android 8+; older devices fall back to an unencrypted java.util.zip engine.) - **`mp_apk_*` tools** — the specialty: list installed apps and available APK files, open an APK by path or package into an edit session, analyze it (manifest, permissions, components, dex list, signing/certificates), decompile single classes to Java with jadx, class outlines and cross-references, list/edit/add/delete/copy entries and string resources (ARSCLib), then rebuild (zipalign) and sign. The source APK is never modified: edits go to a session copy and builds are written to the home folder's `output/` directory. - **`mp_apk_native_*` tools** — native library analysis without any external dependency: a pure-Java ELF parser (inspect, sections, segments, symbols, imports, .rodata strings, address↔offset mapping) and a built-in ARM64 + ARM32/Thumb instruction decoder for disassembly, call/branch overviews and cross-reference scans (x86 falls back to raw bytes). In-place patching of native strings and raw bytes writes back into the session APK for the normal build/sign flow. - **`mp_apk_ssl_unpin`** — patch an APK to bypass SSL pinning (see the SSL Unpinning tool below), callable straight from the conversation. - **`structuredContent`** accompanies every tool result for modern MCP clients. Security model (MT Manager style): the **home folder** (default `/storage/emulated/0/MP Manager/mcp`, configurable) always has read/write access; everything else follows ordered path rules (read-only / read-write / deny, first match wins) managed in the service settings — the AI can query but never elevate them. With no matching rule, shared storage is read-only and everything else is denied. Optional **bearer-token auth** is supported (off by default, like MT Manager); auth does not encrypt traffic, so use a trusted network and never expose the port to the internet. A foreground notification keeps the service alive and can stop it.
SSL Unpinning Patch an APK to **bypass SSL certificate pinning** — inspired by Frida unpinning script collections like [frida-hook-engine](https://github.com/muhammadrizwan87/frida-hook-engine), but implemented as an offline dex patch so the result is a normal standalone APK: no root, no Frida, no Xposed needed. The tool neutralizes in the app's own code: - every class implementing `javax.net.ssl.X509TrustManager`: `checkServerTrusted`/`checkClientTrusted` become no-ops (catches all custom/pinning trust managers, including renamed classes, via interface detection); - OkHttp's `CertificatePinner` (and legacy `com.squareup.okhttp`): `check`/`check$okhttp` become no-ops; - OkHttp's `OkHostnameVerifier` and every class implementing `javax.net.ssl.HostnameVerifier`: `verify(...)` returns true; - every `WebViewClient`: `onReceivedSslError` calls `SslErrorHandler.proceed()` instead of cancelling. Find it in the APK info dialog's "More" menu, the Tools hub, or via the MCP tool `mp_apk_ssl_unpin`. The source APK is untouched; output is saved as `-unpinned.apk` next to it, optionally signed with your signing key. Limitations: framework-level validation (`TrustManagerImpl`) and pinning done inside native `.so` libraries cannot be patched from the APK, and interception tools also need the app to trust user CAs. Use responsibly: only on apps you own or are authorized to test (security research, debugging your own traffic).
### Utilities
Plugins and tool packs Plugins are installed as regular Android apps and listed in the Plugins hub, together with tool packs that can be downloaded inside the app. A plugin can add entries to the sidebar, settings, file menu, text editor or the APK dialog, and each plugin runs in its own process with its own permissions, so it cannot read files unless storage access is granted to it. On first use the certificate fingerprint is confirmed against the one published by the developer, and a warning is shown if it ever changes. Plugins can be trusted, disabled, updated, removed from the hub, or given a launcher shortcut. Tool packs ship collections of tools grouped into Media, Device, Network, Math, Text and Code, Notes and Random packs, covering among others a tone generator, metronome, recorder with screen recording, text to speech, device information, sensors, compass, bubble level, wallpaper maker, QR generator, a calculator suite with converters, text and code tools, and random generators. The pack catalog can be refreshed, packs can be updated or removed, and the server hosting packs can be changed.
Screen color picker [Use a floating overlay to find out colors anywhere on the screen.](https://github.com/codehasan/ScreenColorPicker)


Configuration dialog ·  Picking color

Layout inspector [Inspect the view hierarchy of any app through a floating overlay window.](https://github.com/AbdurazaaqMohammed/Layout-Inspector)


Layout Inspection

Command Helper Command Helper is a simple but powerful tool. It allows you to create templates for commands that can then be quickly applied to any file you select. It can generate commands for several files at once, preview them, and copy or run them directly in Termux, one by one or all at once. A placeholder help documents the variables that can be used in a template. * In this way you can quickly run command line tools like dex2c etc. on files via MP Manager


Creating a command profile  ·  The generated command

Wi-Fi Manager Shows the current connection with link speed, gateway, IP and MAC details, together with data usage for the device and the app. Saved Wi-Fi passwords can be read with root, searched, exported or shared, including as a QR code. Private DNS can be switched between saved profiles with one tap using root or WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS, and a quick settings tile cycles the profiles.
Storage Manager Shows mounted volumes with used and free space, the space used by files grouped by type, and the largest files on the device, which can be filtered by type and deleted. App caches can be listed and cleared with root or accessibility service.
Appearance and storage info Choose between system, light, dark and black theme all with Material theme and Dynamic Colors. A custom font can be picked for the app and a separate one for dialogs. The file list size, the number of lines shown for file names and the date and time format can be changed, folder size can be shown in the file list (always, only in archives, or never), a different startup folder can be set for each pane, and a .bak backup can be created before editing a file. The sidebar shows mounted storages with used and free space available, with app icon, refreshable volumes and organizable entries. The app language can be picked manually (Russian, Simplified Chinese, Spanish, Indonesian, Arabic, Persian and Thai translation currently available) and the app can toggle automatic check for updates.


The sidebar with storage usage

## Why is AI used to develop MP Manager? I had the idea for MP Manager almost 10 years ago and I planned and developed it for years with little progress. I did not even post it on GitHub for a long time because the app barely worked at all. With AI, I was able to advance the app massively in a short time. While some people use arguments like "AI only helps unskilled people" as insults, I believe MP Manager is an example of how AI can be used by regular people to create working alternatives to paid/closed source software. Big corporations love AI because they can save huge money from it, but they **want you and me** to hate AI because it allows regular people to not only save money, but create our own alternatives catered to our needs. So far I used only free AI in development of MP Manager. You can use AI to directly contribute to the development of MP Manager yourself. Some free AI services have referral program that can give me more free usage, you can help me by sign up for these programs with my referral code/link: * [WorkBuddy](https://workbuddy.ai/invite?code=KGGFX6GZ) gives free monthly credits and limited free promotions with models like DeepSeek 4.1 Flash, GLM5.3 Flash, MiniMax M3.1 Flash and more available. * You have to download the program and send at least one message (no charge) for me to get credits. * [ZCode](https://zcode.z.ai/invite/CW3JK87H) offers GLM 5.3/Flash with regular free promotions like 500 million free tokens on weekends. * You have to download the program and complete onboarding (no charge) for me to get credits. * If the app gets more pull requests it may become eligible for the free [Claude for Open Source](https://claude.com/contact-sales/claude-for-oss) program
